title: comparison-standard
description: The relation or predicate that fixes what a predicatory comparison is checking - sameness, containment, strengthening, confluence, or residual difference. It is part of the mathematical data of a comparison context; two contexts over the same inputs but different standards define different comparison morphisms.

family.description: the standard family: exact (equality of valuations/composites, equalization loci), order ($\leq_k$ containment, $\leq_t$ strengthening), residual (evidence to add along a defined direction), confluence (common successor by allowed operations), or temporal (one stage, an interval, or after closure)

relation.description: the relation or predicate the standard applies to the two compared settlings to decide the question

determines-question.description: the standard makes the comparison well-specified: it decides what counts as sameness, divergence, containment, truth-strengthening, joinability, or residual difference
